legend: Sporadic or germline activating mutations in GNAS result in the constitutive activation of Gsα, which upregulates adenylyl cyclase, resulting in increased cAMP, causing the phosphorylation of CREB and the synthesis of growth hormone and α-subunit. In patients with Carney complex, mutations inactivating PRKAR1A have the same effect by enhancing CREB activation. Tumours with these alterations have a densely granulated phenotype and respond well to somatostatin analogue therapy that reduces cAMP. In contrast, changes shown on the right, including AIP mutation or silencing, GHR inactivation, or other mechanisms of reducing STAT signalling, result in sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours that have fibrous bodies.

legend: Scattered fibrous bodies in the background of predominant perinuclear CAM5.2 expression in a densely granulated somatotroph tumour. The term “intermediate-type somatotroph tumour” has been proposed for a subset of densely granulated somatotroph tumours that display occasional fibrous bodies. These tumours are considered within the morphological spectrum of densely granulated somatotroph tumours.
Enhanced T1-weighted MRI. Densely granulated somatotroph tumour.
Plain T2-weighted MRI. Densely granulated somatotroph tumours often show T2 hypointensity.
Enhanced T1-weighted MRI. Sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours tend to be invasive macrotumours (Knosp 4 in this case).
Plain T2-weighted MRI. Sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours tend to be invasive macrotumours (Knosp 4 in this case) that often show T2 hyperintensity.
A densely granulated somatotroph tumour showing diffuse strong reactivity for SSTR2. This patient had a good response to first-line somatostatin analogues.

legend: This densely granulated somatotroph tumour is composed of cells that have abundant eosinophilic (acidophilic) cytoplasm.
Densely granulated somatotroph tumour showing diffuse positivity for growth hormone, a finding consistent with the dense content of growth hormone–containing secretory granules in these tumours.
Unlike sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours, densely granulated somatotroph tumours are often positive for α-subunit.
Densely granulated somatotroph tumours show predominant perinuclear reactivity for CAM5.2.

Sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours are composed of cells with chromophobic to pale eosinophilic cytoplasm. One of the characteristics of these tumours is the presence of abundant fibrous bodies. In this photomicrograph, these eosinophilic globular fibrous bodies indent the tumour nuclei.
Growth hormone expression is often reduced in sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours, consistent with their sparse granulation pattern.
Unlike in densely granulated somatotroph tumours, CAM5.2 staining shows predominant (> 70%) fibrous bodies in sparsely granulated somatotroph tumours.
This densely granulated somatotroph tumour is composed of acidophilic (eosinophilic) tumour cells with abundant growth hormone-containing secretory granules.
